language.name: English
language.about:
DropLaunch's texts in English (built into DropLaunch). To translate: save a copy (Settings, Language), set code (like "nl") and name (like "Nederlands"), and change the text after each key. Keep {placeholders} as they are, and the tags , , , ,
and around the same words. Keys ending in .one and .other are counts (one map / 3 maps). Lines you leave out stay English. Then drop the file on DropLaunch.exe or its window, or put it next to DropLaunch.exe. A file with code "en" next to the exe changes the English texts themselves.

strings.settings.reset.note: Back to how DropLaunch was when you downloaded it: every setting, no folders linked, the welcome screen and setup again. Nothing is deleted.
strings.settings.reset.title: Reset DropLaunch's settings?
strings.settings.reset.text: Every setting goes back to its default, and no folders stay linked: no server, no maps folder, no map history. Bug reports are put aside, so their numbers start at #1 again. DropLaunch then starts like it was just downloaded, with the welcome screen and setup (setup finds SteamCMD and the server files again if they're still there). Nothing is deleted: server files, maps, kits and the put-aside bug reports stay on the disk.

strings.guide.offToast: Tips are off. Settings → Guide turns them back on.
strings.tip.setupDownloads.title: Two downloads
strings.tip.setupDownloads.text: SteamCMD is Valve's tool for downloading game servers ({steamcmd}). It fetches Rust's dedicated server, {server}: a separate program from your Rust game that runs your maps, here on this PC.
strings.tip.setupFramework.text: It lets the server load plugins. Not sure? Pick Carbon. Maps that use RustEdit features, and DropLaunch's bug reports, need Carbon or Oxide.
strings.tip.setupOwner.title: You as the owner
strings.tip.setupOwner.text: The owner is admin on your test servers: fly around with noclip, teleport, spawn items. Press Detect my Steam IDs and pick your account or put it here manually.
strings.tip.setupGo.title: Ready when you are
strings.tip.setupGo.text: Downloads the server and sets it up with the options you picked. Most of the time goes into the server download ({server}); you can hide this window meanwhile.
strings.tip.setupRunning.title: This runs by itself
strings.tip.setupRunning.text: Depending on your internet connection it takes 5 to 30 minutes. Hide keeps it going in the background, and the Maps page shows the progress.
strings.tip.checklist.title: Your next steps
strings.tip.checklist.text: This list ticks itself off as you go. Tips like this one show once each; Settings → Guide turns them off.
strings.tip.maps.title: Your maps
strings.tip.maps.text: Maps in your Maps folder show up here, both new or updated maps appear by themselves.
strings.tip.start.title: Start a server
strings.tip.start.text: Press ▶ on a map (or double-click it) to run that map on a Rust server. The first start of a map takes a bit longer.
strings.tip.start.textMore: Start server runs the selected map on a Rust server. The first start of a map takes a bit longer.
strings.tip.booting.title: Starting up
strings.tip.booting.text: Server is loading its files and building the map: a few minutes the first time, faster after that. The steps show the progress, and DropLaunch tells you if it might be stuck.
strings.tip.ready.title: Your server is ready
strings.tip.ready.text: Opens Rust and connects you to the server automatically. Or press F1 in Rust and type the connect command shown here.
strings.tip.joined.title: You're on your own server
strings.tip.joined.text: Saved the map again in RustEdit? Restart loads the new version. Make yourself the owner (Mods, owner & start files) to fly around with noclip.
strings.tip.joined.textOwner: As the owner you can press F1 in Rust and type noclip to fly around. Saved the map again in RustEdit? Restart loads the new version.
strings.tip.stop.title: When you're done
strings.tip.stop.text: Stop saves and ends the server. Closing DropLaunch leaves the server running (DropLaunch finds it again next time).
strings.tip.crashed.title: It didn't start
strings.tip.crashed.text: The message says why. More options shown in the server's console with its whole log.
strings.tip.more.text: Shows the server console, performance graphs, and the Server files page: updates, mods and folders.
strings.tip.update.title: A server update
strings.tip.update.text: Your Rust game and the server need the same version to connect. Rust updates every month, sometimes in between: update the server files when this shows.
strings.tip.bugSwitch.text: Tick this to add DropLaunch's small plugin to your servers. It's needed for bug reports.
strings.tip.bugChat.title: Send a report
strings.tip.bugChat.text: In Rust, open the chat and type /bug and what's wrong. It shows up here, and on a map of your server where you stood, with the option to teleport there.
strings.tip.kits.text: Kits are sets of items for anyone on your server, you included: pick one and press Give to. Basic Build Kit comes with DropLaunch: a building plan, a hammer, code locks, doors, a tool cupboard and plenty of materials. Full screen lets you make your own.
strings.tip.bugs.title: Your bug reports
strings.tip.bugs.text: Each /bug from Rust's chat lands here, the newest first. Open them for a map of the server with a pin where each one was sent: see what the tester was looking at, mark it fixed, or teleport there.

strings.about.intro: DropLaunch is built with these open-source libraries, under their own licenses. Click one for its notice and license text.
strings.about.downloadedText: Not part of DropLaunch: it gets them from their makers, under their own terms. SteamCMD and the Rust server (Valve, Facepunch, through Steam), Carbon (GPL-3.0), Oxide (MIT), the RustEdit extension (k1lly0u), and the item pictures in Kits (Facepunch's artwork, from wiki.rustclash.com or cdn.rusthelp.com the first time they're shown).
